reviewNotes: HOLD. First-party China Telecom (Macau) FAQ clears the final lifecycle blocker: Greater Bay Area prepaid is valid 180 days from activation; recharging resets validity to 180 days from the recharge date; zero balance/expiry suspends service and >90 days suspended cancels the card. Current Easy PASS material confirms real-name registration, Macau mobile number, free incoming SMS in Macau/mainland China/Hong Kong, and current eSIM support. A Sep 2026 independent report reproduces physical-to-eSIM conversion and MOP50/180-day normal retention. Admit backstage HOLD because service-specific bank/app OTP reliability remains insufficiently sampled.

events.outcome: Current provider FAQ states Greater Bay Area prepaid is valid 180 days from activation; a recharge during validity extends/reset validity to 180 days from the recharge date; zero balance or expiry suspends service; more than 90 days continuously suspended causes automatic cancellation.

Current provider eSIM center lists Easy Pass as a prepaid eSIM product and supports designated physical-SIM-to-eSIM conversion for eligible existing customers; a September 2026 independent user report reproduces successful conversion.

Current Easy PASS brochure states incoming SMS is free in Macau, mainland China and Hong Kong. This proves ordinary incoming-SMS capability only; service-specific bank/app OTP reliability remains unverified in this review.

data.acquisitionSummary: China Telecom (Macau) Easy PASS / Greater Bay Area prepaid is a no-fixed-monthly-fee Macau-number route for mainland China, Macau and Hong Kong. Current provider material requires real-name registration and supports physical/eSIM use; provider FAQ lists China Telecom stores, Macau phone shops and the Aomi app China Telecom section as prepaid purchase channels.

keep.action: Recharge before the 180-day validity expires. China Telecom (Macau) officially states any recharge during validity resets/extends the prepaid-card validity to 180 days from the recharge date. A September 2026 independent report reproduces MOP50 as the normal recharge/keep action; treat MOP50 as community-observed, not an official minimum guarantee.

data.chinaActivation: Real-name registration is required before use. Current provider material supports mainland-China use and current eSIM conversion, but this review does not claim every device can be activated remotely from mainland China without setup friction.
data.kyc: Required. The current Easy PASS brochure says the phone card must be real-name registered before use and provides the China Telecom Macau real-name flow.
data.payment: Provider brochure documents top-up through the China Telecom Macau WeChat official account plus supported electronic payment methods and Macau recharge cards; payment availability can vary by channel.
data.roamingSms: Current provider brochure states incoming SMS is free while in Macau, mainland China and Hong Kong. Bank/app OTP delivery is not guaranteed by that statement and remains HOLD.
data.holdReason: Lifecycle, recharge reset, real-name, incoming-SMS capability and current eSIM support are verified, but recent bank/app-specific OTP outcomes are not sufficiently sampled for recommendation status.
data.tariffSummary: No fixed monthly fee. Provider-verified 180-day card validity with another 180 days from each recharge; >90 days continuously suspended cancels the card. Community-observed normal keep action is MOP50 per 180 days.
guideSteps: Acquire a current Easy PASS / Greater Bay Area prepaid product and complete real-name registration.
Before day 180, make a recharge and confirm the returned validity date; do not assume a lower recharge floor than your channel accepts.
Test each critical bank/app verification flow before binding an important account; ordinary incoming SMS capability is not an OTP guarantee.
